inputs.drivers: Allied rearmament; affordable autonomous mass; acquisition reform; founder alignment; talent; patient private capital; retained IP; software reuse; manufacturing scale; Ukraine and Indo-Pacific lessons; export and budget constraints.
inputs.invalidation: Founder or governance risk, scaling failure, network access mistaken for demand, bespoke requirements, inventory and capital risk, program delays, safety failures, cash burn, concentration, or excessive private valuation.
inputs.seed_claim: Anduril may represent a defence product-company model shift through privately funded R&D, retained IP, off-the-shelf systems, reusable Lattice autonomy, and Arsenal manufacturing, but public exposure remains indirect before an IPO.
inputs.supporting_evidence: The seed requires funded programs, audited growth, repeat production, recurring software or service economics, credible IPO preparation, and material pull-through for listed partners such as PLTR, ACHR, or suppliers.
inputs.value_chain: Defence product companies; autonomy software; autonomous systems; counter-UAS; attritable weapons; software-defined manufacturing; tactical compute, sensors, communications; listed partners and legacy-prime substitutes.

objective: Research one Anduril defence product-company and future-IPO investment idea.
